title: NCW security self-test evidence artifact
description: The artifact written by `occ ncw_tools:security:selftest --output=json`, and logged as the structured context of the `ncw_tools security selftest` line. It is the C5 PSS-07 evidence that this instance hashes passwords with argon2id. The shape is a cross-repo contract: nc-manager/bin/send-report.sh reads it with jq and forwards it to the report endpoint, so a change to it needs a schema_version bump. No field ever carries hash material, a salt or a secret value - only algorithm names, counts, booleans and cost parameters.

schema_version.$comment: A string, not a number. Bump on any change to this schema.

timestamp.description: Collection time, always UTC with a literal Z, from gmdate('Y-m-d\TH:i:s\Z').

result.description: PASS only when both password_hashing.result and security_config.result are PASS.

instance.description: Self-describing instance identity. Every field may be an empty string: id and url come from IConfig and name/namespace/environment from the deployment's environment variables, which the chart only sets for the self-test Job.

url.description: overwrite.cli.url from IConfig; the downstream fallback identifier.

name.description: INSTANCE_NAME. Arbitrary bytes from the environment, substituted to valid UTF-8 by the producer.

namespace.description: NAMESPACE, set by the chart from the downward API.

configured_algorithm.description: The algorithm a *new* password gets, from hashing a random probe through IHasher and classifying the result. Must be argon2id to pass.

stored_distribution.description: Row counts per algorithm over the surveyed rows of the users table. The four required buckets are always present; argon2i, legacy-bcrypt and legacy-sha1 appear only when rows of that kind are actually observed, so their presence is itself the finding. Read named keys or sum to_entries - do not assume a fixed key set.

allOf.$comment: A passing hashing section pins what it means: argon2id configured, no round-trip failure, and not one surveyed row outside the tolerated argon2id/empty buckets.

checks.description: One entry per asserted config value, read through IConfig so the effective merged configuration is asserted rather than a single file. The list is extensible: consumers must match on key rather than on position or length.
checks.$comment: Currently: hashing_default_password, auth.bruteforce.protection.enabled, ratelimit.protection.enabled, overwriteprotocol, passwordsalt_present, secret_present.

key.description: The config key, or <key>_present where only the presence of a secret may be reported.

parameters.description: Evidence, not an assertion: the cost parameters the probe hash was actually produced with, as reported by password_get_info(). memory_cost/time_cost/threads for argon2, cost for bcrypt. These are the effective values, which is stronger evidence than the hashing* config keys because the hasher clamps those to the algorithm minimums. An empty object when the parameters cannot be read - notably for an argon2 hash on a PHP build without argon2 support, where only the registered handler could read the cost fields.
parameters.$comment: Always a JSON object, never []. The producer casts the map so an empty one cannot degrade into an array on either evidence channel.

allOf.$comment: A top-level PASS cannot be claimed while either section fails.

verdict.description: A section or overall verdict. SKIPPED is only ever a round_trip result.

algorithm.description: The classes OCA\NcwTools\Security\HashAlgorithm reports. bcrypt/argon2i carry a hasher version prefix; the legacy-* forms are unprefixed; empty means no local password (an SSO-only account); unknown means the value matched no known algorithm marker.

checkValue.description: Config assertions are booleans or strings only. A secret is reported as a boolean under <key>_present - never as its value.

roundTrip.description: The optional live proof: a disposable ncw-selftest-<random> user is created through IUserManager, its stored hash read back, and the user deleted again. SKIPPED unless --round-trip is given, and a skipped round trip never affects any result.

stored_algorithm.description: The algorithm classified from the row the probe user actually wrote; null when the probe could not be created, and always null when SKIPPED.

cleaned_up.description: Re-checked after deletion by resolving the uid again. null only when SKIPPED.

allOf.$comment: A skipped round trip reports nothing at all.
A round trip that ran always knows whether it cleaned up after itself.
PASS is only reachable with argon2id stored and the probe user gone.
